For a renter, I’d choose a **portable power station with a separate panel**, rather than a kit that plugs into your apartment’s wiring. The panel sits on the balcony and charges the battery; you bring the battery indoors to power devices.

**Simple, compact pick:** [BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W solar panel kit](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2-100w-solar-kit) — listed at **$489.99**. Its 288 Wh battery is suited to phones, a laptop, a router, or a fan; it **won’t run a fridge**. ([Dealectric’s kit guide](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-kit-for-an-apartment-balcony))

If you want more capacity for an outage, the [Anker SOLIX C800X](https://powerbencher.com/stories/home-backup/best-portable-power-stations-apartment/) is a larger option listed at 960 Wh and 1,500 W, with balcony solar recharging in mind. You’d need to match it with a compatible panel.

Before setting up, check your lease and building rules, secure the panel so it can’t fall or blow away, and keep it clear of walkways. These are **off-grid charging setups**—don’t connect a power station to your apartment’s wiring.

judge.top_pick: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W Solar Panel Kit
products: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W Solar Panel Kit
judge.why: The answer leads with our BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W kit, with its price and specs taken from dealectric.com and linked to its balcony guide, but no concern was given, so point_carried is false.
